business_problem: Midea IoT depended on an ELK-based device-log pipeline that was becoming hard to scale as connected-device volume and analysis demand rose. The architecture involved too many hops, separate data silos for real-time, offline, and monitoring use cases, and a heavy self-managed Elasticsearch footprint.
solution_summary: Midea IoT rebuilt its observability and log-analysis backbone on Alibaba Cloud with SLS as the unified data substrate and STAROps as the AI operations hub. Filebeat was replaced by LoongCollector for direct collection into SLS, Kafka-originated business data is ingested through SLS write processors, and the same data base supports real-time query, subscription consumption, and offline archiving rather than copying logs across several systems. Offline data is compressed into MaxCompute, while OSS and unified data APIs replace much of the old Elasticsearch dependency. On top of the new log architecture, STAROps combines cross-domain observability data with large-language-model reasoning and AI-friendly Skills, CLI tools, and agents so internal monitoring teams can perform natural-language query and root-cause analysis directly against the new substrate. The result is a serverless, lower-ops observability platform that scales with IoT growth.

solution_components.name: Log Service SLS
solution_components.role: Acts as the unified ingest, query, consumption, and archival substrate for device logs.

solution_components.name: LoongCollector
solution_components.role: Collects logs directly into SLS in place of Filebeat-based ingestion.

solution_components.name: MaxCompute
solution_components.role: Receives offline compressed archives and supports large-scale analysis on historical log data.

solution_components.name: STAROps
solution_components.role: Provides AI-assisted natural-language query and root-cause analysis on top of unified observability data.

data_flow: Device logs and business Kafka data are collected into SLS through LoongCollector and SLS write processors, then exposed through APIs, subscriptions, and direct platform reads for monitoring and analysis. Historical data is archived into MaxCompute and OSS, while STAROps reasons over the cross-domain observability data for natural-language analysis and incident diagnosis.
business_outcome: Midea IoT eliminated much of the self-managed ELK overhead and replaced it with a serverless observability substrate that is easier to scale with device growth. Query speed improved, self-built ES clusters and cleaning services were retired, and AI-assisted operations became a native capability of the log platform rather than a separate tool.
metrics: device-log query and bulk data retrieval efficiency improved 50%
self-built ES clusters and log-cleaning services were fully retired
architecture_clues: SLS is treated as the single data substrate for real-time query, subscription, and archive flows instead of duplicating logs into multiple systems.
STAROps is tightly integrated with Midea's internal monitoring systems so natural-language query and diagnosis work on the same unified data base.
Historical archives are pushed into MaxCompute and OSS instead of being left in a hot-search cluster indefinitely.
